lines: I hear your apology. Show me what changes next.
Remorse matters when it leads to repair.
I accept the words, though trust will return slowly.
Thank you for saying it plainly.
An apology cannot undo the harm, but it can begin the work.
I believe you regret it. Now make it right.
Do not promise perfection. Promise better judgment.
I needed to hear that from you.
Let your next choice prove these words.
Forgiveness does not mean forgetting what happened.
I can meet you halfway if you come honestly.
The wound is closed. The lesson should remain.
I accept your apology without pretending everything is settled.
Give me time, and keep your word.
Owning the mistake is better than defending it.
We can move forward after the damage is repaired.
I would rather see changed behavior than repeated regret.
Thank you. That sounded difficult to admit.
I am willing to try again carefully.
Your apology is a start. Let it be a good one.
